minutes.headline: Commission issued an order of conditions for Hickory Hills Dam work, waiving wetland replication as non-significant
minutes.summary: The Commission heard a drone consultant presentation, then ran hearings: negative determinations for a house lot and a parking lot, an order of conditions for the Hickory Hills Dam overtopping project, and continuances for four others. It discussed the Lake Shirley management report, including data gaps and the water clarity threshold, then heard the small-town forest harvest update and a police ATV funding request.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the applicant was tenant or owner at the Electric Avenue hearing.
Asked about plantings along the 30 foot no-disturb zone at Electric Avenue.
Trails at the small-town forest are hard to follow after logging; asked how they will be marked and restored.
Debris from the harvest is heavy; wants a plan and harvest revenue spent on trails and parking.
Resident urged that harvest revenue go back into trails, signs, parking and maps rather than other purchases such as the ATV.
Residents asked for trail maps and online information; a regional trail coalition offers mapping.
Commission should meet its own needs, such as the small-town forest, before donating to the ATV purchase.
Said the ATV was fully funded in the capital plan.

what_happened.line: The Commission issued a standard order of conditions for the Hickory Hills Dam overtopping project, with no replacement of the lost wetland, noted as non-significant.
Negative determinations were voted for the house and driveway at 221 Goodrich Street and for the 5 Electric Avenue parking lot.
Hearings for 307 Townsend Harbor Road, 548 Northfield Road and 45 Route 12 were continued to March 7.
On the Lake Shirley management report, members agreed a five foot water clarity threshold; the improvement corporation will propose more sampling sites.
Residents asked that small-town forest harvest revenue go back into trails, signs and parking; the Commission took no action on the police ATV request, as it is in the capital plan.

why_it_matters: The dam order allows work to proceed without replacing the wetland lost, which bears on flood protection and wetland habitat near the lake.
The clarity threshold and added sampling sites will shape how Lake Shirley's water quality is measured and judged.
Where timber revenue from the town forest goes decides whether trails and parking there are repaired, and the ATV request is funded through the capital plan, not Commission money.
watch_next: March 7: continued hearings for 307 Townsend Harbor Road, 548 Northfield Road and 45 Route 12.
A site walk for the extension permit project, set before March 7.
